text.p: Pen pictures of the Newcastle United players most likely to play against Middlesbrough in Sunday's English premier league match at St James' Park:

Pavel Srnicek, goalkeeper, age 28. A Czech international who has become something of a folk hero at Newcastle where the fans appreciate his acrobatics and outstanding shot-stopping ability but despair at some of his crazy mistakes.
John Beresford, defender, 30. Consistent defender who likes to get forward but, like the rest of the Newcastle back line, prone to errors. Currently nursing a hamstring injury.

Darren Peacock, defender, 28. At 2.7 million pounds ($4.34 million) was Newcastle's record buy before the arrival of Les Ferdinand, Faustino Asprilla and Alan Shearer. Tall with long, flowing locks, good in the air.

Philip Albert, defender, 29. Belgian international who has regained his place in the side following a ligament injury. Highly skilled as his superbly lobbed goal against Manchester United last week proved. Belgium's Player of the Year 1992.

Warren Barton, defender, 27. London-born Barton, bought from Wimbledon for 4.5 million pounds ($7.2 million) and in the England team 18 months ago, is now out of favour having lost his place to Steve Watson. Been linked with a move to both Tottenham and his boyhood idols, Arsenal.

Steve Watson, defender/midfielder, 22. One of the few locals in the side who did not cost a huge transfer fee. Can operate at the back, in midfield or even up front. An ever-present in the league this season. Was Newcastle's youngest-ever player when he made his debut aged 16 in 1990.
David Batty, midfield, 27. Joined Newcastle in March from Blackburn for 3.5 million pounds ($5.6 million). Combative, hard-tackling, England international who first played for Leeds when he was 18.
Robert Lee, midfield, 30. Made seven appearances for England over last two seasons but Londonder Lee did not make squad for Euro 96. Industrious creative midfielder with an eye for goal.

Peter Beardsley, midfield/striker. Now 35 but as influential as ever. Club captain in his second spell with Newcastle after seven years at Liverpool and Everton. Has scored over 100 goals for the club and is one of their all-time great players. Has 59 England caps.
Lee Clark, midfield, 24. In and out of the side but a reliable midfield anchor who was born locally and signed straight from school.

Faustino Asprilla, forward, 26. Colombian international who signed for 7.5 million pounds ($12 million) last season. Undoubted talent, vision and pace but has found it hard to adapt to English football and has spent most of this season on the bench. Scored twice on return in UEFA Cup on Tuesday.

David Ginola, midfield/forward, 29. French international almost as at home modelling on the cat-walk as ripping apart rival defences. Superb skills, the 1994 French Footballer of the Year is idolised on Tyneside. Scored magnificent individual goal against Ferencvaros in UEFA Cup on Tuesday.

Les Ferdinand, forward, 29. Came into professional soccer relatively late at the age of 21 but has made up for it since. Moved from QPR to Newcastle for six million pounds ($9.6 million) before the start of last season and scored 29 goals in his first campaign. England international.

Keith Gillespie, forward, 21. When Andy Cole moved from Newcastle to Manchester United, he moved to St James' Park as a one-million-pound ($1.65 million) component in the deal. A Northern Ireland international.
Robbie Elliott, defender, 22. Capable local-born youngster who usually impresses whenever he gets in the side.
Paul Kitson, forward, 25. Signed from Derby for 2.25 million pounds ($3.6 million) in October 1994. Has had to be content with a substitute's role for most of the last season and a half.
Shaka Hislop, goalkeeper, 27. A Trinidad youth international who started and finished last season as first choice but who has been restricted to just one appearance this season.
